questions.prompt: What can Go functions do that's used for the (result, error) pattern?
What is Go's core idiom for error handling, per this lesson?

choices.text: Returning `(value, error)` from functions instead of throwing

questions.prompt: When should callers typically check the error returned from a function call?

choices.text: Never, only if the value looks wrong
At the very end of the program

questions.prompt: What is a variadic function, per this lesson?

choices.text: A function that accepts a variable number of arguments of the same type
A function that returns multiple values
A function that can be called without parentheses

questions.prompt: Inside a variadic function, how does the variadic parameter behave?

choices.text: Like a regular slice of that type
As a separate variable for each argument

questions.prompt: Where must a variadic parameter appear in a function's signature?

choices.text: Last, and a function can only have one
It must be the only parameter

questions.prompt: What is a closure, per this lesson?

choices.text: A function that can only run once
A function that captures and remembers variables from the scope it was created in
A function with no return value
A function that can't access variables outside itself

questions.prompt: In the `makeCounter` example, what happens each time `makeCounter()` is called?

choices.text: It reuses the same `count` variable across all counters
It creates a brand new `count` variable, so counters don't interfere with each other
It resets a global counter to 0
It throws an error if called twice

questions.prompt: What does this lesson say closures let Go achieve, that other languages need classes for?

choices.text: Stateful function generators, middleware, and callback handlers

questions.prompt: When does a deferred function call actually run?

choices.text: Right before the enclosing function returns
At a random point during execution

questions.prompt: What order do multiple `defer` calls run in?
What is `defer` most often used for, per this lesson?

choices.text: Cleanup, like closing a file or releasing a lock
